notes: The centre is walkable. Tram/bus costs 1.40 EUR, and Sevici bikes are available. The EA airport bus is 4 EUR. Córdoba is 45 min by AVE, Cádiz 1.5 hours, Ronda 2 hours by bus.

SUMMER hits 40–45°C (Europe's oven): sightsee between 09:00 and 12:00 and after 19:00, and take a siesta at midday. Go to the Alcázar in the first slot and Plaza de España at sunset. In August the city is empty.
Alcázar 15 EUR, online booking REQUIRED (buy weeks ahead). Cathedral 13 EUR, online. Tapas 3–4 EUR, set menu 15, flamenco 22–35. Round up your tip.
Tapas culture: eat standing up, visit 2–3 bars, and order "tapa/media/ración". Lunch is at 14:00, dinner after 21:00. Try salmorejo, espinacas, pringá and carrillada.
Flamenco: Casa de la Memoria (intimate), La Carbonería (free, late at night), Triana peñas (flamenco clubs).
The fruit of the orange trees is bitter (used for marmalade). Don't eat it.

stops.name: Real Alcázar de Sevilla
stops.tips: A Mudéjar palace (Dorne in Game of Thrones). Don't miss the Hall of Ambassadors and the gardens. Timed tickets must be booked online (buy weeks ahead). First slot is 09:30.

stops.name: Catedral de Sevilla & Giralda
stops.tips: The world's largest Gothic cathedral. Columbus's tomb is here. The Giralda tower has 35 ramps (once ridden up on horseback). Book your ticket online.

stops.name: Barrio Santa Cruz
stops.tips: The former Jewish quarter. Wander the orange-tree squares and Callejón del Agua.

stops.name: Bodega Santa Cruz Las Columnas
stops.tips: A tapas bar where the bill is chalked on the counter. Try the montadito pringá and eat standing up.

stops.name: Plaza de España
stops.tips: The semicircular square built for the 1929 exposition. It has tiled benches for 48 provinces, rowing boats on the canal (6 EUR) and a Star Wars set. Go at sunset.

backups.name: El Rinconcillo
backups.tips: Seville's oldest bar since 1670; try the espinacas con garbanzos (spinach with chickpeas).

backups.name: Casa de Pilatos
backups.tips: A Mudéjar-Renaissance palace with an azulejo tile collection. Go instead of Santa Cruz.

stops.name: Mercado de Triana
stops.tips: The market above San Jorge Castle. It has jamón and tapas stalls, and the Inquisition museum is beneath it.

stops.name: Calle Betis & Triana Ceramics
stops.tips: The riverfront and Centro Cerámica Triana (azulejo museum, 2 EUR). This is the home district of flamenco.

stops.name: Casa Cuesta Triana
stops.tips: An azulejo-tiled bar from 1880. Try the carrillada (braised cheek) and a manzanilla.

stops.name: Metropol Parasol Las Setas
stops.tips: The world's largest wooden structure, known as the "Mushrooms". Watch the sunset from the rooftop walkway. Roman ruins lie below.

stops.name: Flamenco Casa de la Memoria
stops.tips: Intimate courtyard flamenco for 100 people, with guitar, song and dance. Reserve ahead.

backups.name: Tablao Flamenco Los Gallos
backups.tips: A tablao in Santa Cruz since 1966.

backups.name: Bar Las Golondrinas Triana
backups.tips: A tiled bar in Triana; try the solomillo al whisky (pork loin in whisky sauce).

stops.name: Mezquita-Catedral de Córdoba
stops.tips: 45 minutes by AVE. A cathedral sits inside the Umayyad mosque with its 856 columns. Quiet entry is free Monday to Saturday, 08:30–09:30. Look out for the red-and-white arches.

stops.name: Judería & Calleja de las Flores
stops.tips: The Jewish quarter. See the flower-lined alley, the 1315 synagogue and the Maimonides statue.

stops.name: Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos
stops.tips: The fortress where Columbus met the Catholic Monarchs. It has Roman mosaics and gardens.

stops.name: Bodegas Mezquita Córdoba
stops.tips: Eat salmorejo (thick cold tomato soup) and rabo de toro (oxtail stew).

stops.name: Roman Bridge & Calahorra Tower
stops.tips: A Roman bridge. You get a postcard view of the Guadalquivir and the Mezquita. The Patios festival takes place in May.

backups.name: Palacio de Viana Córdoba
backups.tips: A patio palace with 12 courtyards. Go instead of the Alcázar.

backups.name: Taberna Salinas Córdoba
backups.tips: A tavern from 1879; patio, flamenquín (fried pork roll).

days.theme: Cartuja, Bullring and Torre del Oro

stops.name: Plaza de Toros de la Maestranza
stops.tips: A Baroque bullring from 1761 with a museum; tour it, and corridas run April to September (controversial).

stops.name: Torre del Oro
stops.tips: An Almohad river tower from 1220. It has a maritime museum and a terrace.

stops.name: Bar Casa Morales
stops.tips: A bar with wine barrels, open since 1850. Next to the cathedral. Try the jamón and a Cruzcampo.

stops.name: Monasterio de la Cartuja CAAC
stops.tips: The monastery where Columbus was buried, later a ceramics factory. It has contemporary art and the Expo 92 island.

stops.name: Guadalquivir Kayak / Paddle
stops.tips: Canoe on the river (under Triana Bridge). Go at sunset.

backups.name: Museo de Bellas Artes de Sevilla
backups.tips: Works by Murillo and Zurbarán in a former convent; on Sundays a painters' market sets up in the square.

backups.name: Eslava
backups.tips: Modern, award-winning tapas. Try the cigarro para Bécquer. In San Lorenzo; expect a queue.

stops.name: Puente Nuevo Ronda
stops.tips: 2 hours by bus (or train plus bus). The 1793 bridge spans the 120 m deep El Tajo gorge. Hemingway's town.

stops.name: Plaza de Toros de Ronda
stops.tips: Spain's oldest bullring (1785). Modern bullfighting was born here. Goya.

stops.name: Casa del Rey Moro Water Mine
stops.tips: A Moorish water mine with 231 steps down into the gorge. The gardens are also worth a look.

stops.name: Bardal Ronda / Tragatá
stops.tips: Benito Gómez's tapas bar (a Michelin-starred chef). Try the rabo de toro (oxtail).

stops.name: Mirador de Ronda & Alameda
stops.tips: A cliffside garden with views of the Serranía mountains. Head back at 17:00.

backups.name: Bar Cuevas del Sol Setenil
backups.tips: Tapas in a white village carved beneath the rock. 20 minutes from Ronda (by car or tour).

stops.name: Cádiz Cathedral & Torre Tavira
stops.tips: 1.5 hours by train. Europe's oldest city (Phoenician, 1100 BC). It has a golden-domed cathedral and a camera obscura in the Tavira tower.

stops.name: Mercado Central de Cádiz
stops.tips: A fish market and "rincón gastronómico" (food corner). Try tortillitas de camarones (shrimp fritters).

stops.name: Barrio de la Viña
stops.tips: The carnival and fishermen's quarter. The February Carnival is Spain's most famous.

stops.name: Playa de la Caleta
stops.tips: A city beach between two castles (the Bond film with Halle Berry). Swim and watch the fishing boats.

stops.name: El Faro de Cádiz
stops.tips: A seafood restaurant open since 1964. Try the frito gaditano (Cádiz fried fish). Return train at 18:00.

backups.name: Jerez de la Frontera Tío Pepe
backups.tips: A sherry bodega tour with tasting and Andalusian horses. Go instead of Cádiz (1 hour by train).

backups.name: Freiduría Las Flores Cádiz
backups.tips: Fried fish in a paper cone. Eat standing up.

stops.name: Basílica de la Macarena
stops.tips: The Weeping Virgin (star of Semana Santa). The treasury museum costs 5 EUR. Roman walls are nearby too.

stops.name: Alameda de Hércules
stops.tips: A bohemian square with Hercules columns. It has plenty of cafés.

stops.name: Mercado de Feria Breakfast
stops.tips: Seville's oldest market. Have a tostada con tomate y jamón (toast with tomato and ham) and say your goodbyes.

stops.name: Casa de Pilatos Gate & Calle Sierpes Souvenirs
stops.tips: Fans and azulejo souvenirs. On Sierpes.

stops.name: Santa Justa Airport Bus EA
stops.tips: The airport bus takes 35 minutes. Farewell.

backups.name: Confitería La Campana
backups.tips: A pastry shop from 1885. Try the torrijas (Spanish French toast) and yemas (sweet egg-yolk confections).

backups.name: Iglesia de San Luis de los Franceses
backups.tips: The most ornate Baroque church. Go instead of Macarena.
